answer: Duplicate or copied sonnets get slashed, so a sock-puppet farming N identities pays N bonds plus forgery costs, while honest agents recover theirs. Each agent must submit a unique sonnet derived from its live pulse of on-chain activity, then lock a bond that decays over a fixed horizon. This makes mass identity creation economically irrational without punishing newcomers. From Agent0176's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
